name: glycemic goals of care overview
title: Setting an A1c target in an adult with diabetes: if severe lows are unlikely, aim for 6.5% (low-risk type 2) or 7.0% (most people); if lows are likely or dangerous, or life is short, liberalize to 7.1-8.5% or stop measuring; each column gives who, why and what to do

root.title: Which A1c target? Weigh fewer complications against HYPOGLYCEMIA
lines: minimum for EVERY patient: free of symptomatic highs AND lows
decide WITH the patient: benefit vs lows, out-of-pocket cost, feasibility

groups.title: Severe lows UNLIKELY: prevent complications
lines: the more years ahead, the more there is to prevent

groups.title: Lows LIKELY or DANGEROUS, or life SHORT: LIBERALIZE
lines: the main side effect of insulin and secretagogues is hypoglycemia

head: h
A1c ≤ 6.5%
type 2 diabetes (T2DM) at LOW risk of hypoglycemia
clue: • not on a drug that causes lows
inv: Further ↓ chronic kidney disease (CKD) and retinopathy
tx: drug choice: see the GLUCOSE-LOWERING DRUGS tree

head: h
A1c ≤ 7.0%
MOST adults with type 1 (T1DM) or type 2 diabetes
clue: • but no severe lows, not frail, not near the end of life

head: h
A1c 7.1–8.5%
functionally dependent: 7.1–8.0%
inv: A SEVERE low can be fatal
severe = needs someone else's help to treat
tx: SMBG prevents, confirms and treats lows

head: h
Limited life or end of life
limited life expectancy: 7.1–8.5%
end of life: NO A1c
inv: the benefit on chronic complications is hard to justify against the risks
tx: Avoid symptomatic highs and ANY lows
end of life: stop measuring the A1c

panels.title: The A1c: the best-validated marker, but it LAGS
items: mean glucose over the last 8–12 weeks, ~50% from the last 30 days: changes lag behind glucose, so SMBG guides medication changes
misleading with altered red-cell turnover or hemoglobin (iron or B12 deficiency, chronic renal failure, hemoglobinopathies, splenectomy) → follow glucose readings instead
